title: Build conv2d and its backward pass from im2col
brief: Lay every window out as a column, multiply by the flattened kernels, then write col2im as a scatter-add and build dx, dw, and db. Gradients are checked against finite differences.
hints: im2col needs a loop over the k * k kernel offsets only, not over output positions. For offset (dh, dw), x_padded[:, :, dh:dh + stride * h_out:stride, dw:dw + stride * w_out:stride] holds that offset's value for every output position at once.

Store the slices in an array of shape (N, C, k, k, H_out, W_out), then reshape to (N, C * k * k, H_out * W_out). The reshape flattens in (channel, kernel row, kernel column) order, which matches w.reshape(C_out, -1).
conv2d_forward: np.einsum('oc,ncl->nol', w.reshape(C_out, -1), col) + b[None, :, None], then reshape to (N, C_out, H_out, W_out).
conv1x1_as_matmul: flatten the spatial axes with x.reshape(N, C_in, H * W), multiply by w.reshape(C_out, C_in) on the left, add b[:, None], and reshape back.

col2im mirrors im2col: reshape dcol to (N, C, k, k, H_out, W_out), then for each kernel offset add dcol_r[:, :, dh, dw] into the same strided slice of a zero padded canvas. Use += because windows overlap, and when padding is 0 return the canvas as it is: canvas[:, :, 0:-0] is empty.
window_coverage is col2im applied to an array of ones with the shape im2col would produce for a single one-channel image.

conv2d_backward: db = dY_mat.sum(axis=(0, 2)); dw_mat = einsum('nol,ncl->oc', dY_mat, col); dcol = einsum('oc,nol->ncl', w_mat, dY_mat); then dx = col2im(dcol, ...). Reshape dw_mat back to the shape of w.
